name: Search and recall
summary: Finding memory: keyword and semantic search, reranking, relational recall, learned ranking, recall benchmarks and session history.

features.name: Vault search
features.summary: Full-text search over notes and brain memory with explanations, compact cards, drill-down and a recall gate.
capabilities: Fuses keyword and vector lanes by weighted sum (0.6/0.4) or rank fusion with k=60 (`search_fusion_mode`)
Boosts results by inbound links, Weibull recency, entities, tier and logged access
Diversifies the ranked list by maximal marginal relevance (lambda 0.7)
Filters by path, property, chunk kind, link degree, event time, visibility and owner
Returns full chunks or 240-char cards that `search expand` and `brain_search_expand` page into the note
`explain` adds per-result score breakdowns (MCP) and, only with the trust gate on, a decision trace
Shortlists the notes worth reading by multi-hop link BFS without reading them (`search plan`)
Judges by prompt shape whether recall should run, without searching (`brain_recall_gate`)
limits: Only the FTS5 keyword lane runs until an embedding provider is configured and `search_semantic_enabled` is on
The recall gate's adequacy verdict needs caller-supplied scores and match quality
`pretool-orient` blocks a first raw vault read only in Claude Code and OpenCode, with `hook_strict_enabled`
Lane weights, `--source` and `--expand` are CLI-only; the served MCP schema omits them

features.name: Search index
features.summary: Builds, refreshes, rebuilds, watches and diagnoses the local full-text index that search reads.
capabilities: Indexes vault Markdown into SQLite FTS5 (BM25) in 800-token chunks with 100 overlap; frontmatter is chunk 0
Updates the index incrementally and skips files whose content did not change (`search index`)
Rebuilds the index from scratch, parking the previous one as `.bak` or `.old` (`search reindex`)
At server or session start, repairs in a detached run an index that no in-place schema upgrade can fix
Re-indexes edited `.md` files 800 ms after a change while `search watch` runs
Starts one detached index run when a read finds the index older than `search_freshen_interval_s` (60 s)
Upgrades an index on an older schema in place, keeping its embeddings, before reporting it (`search status`)
Checks the vault, index folder, SQLite FTS5, vector extension, embedding key and provider (`search check`)
Resolves the event anchors of documents indexed before anchors existed, dry run unless `--apply`
Writes or drift-checks the JSON Schema of the search query language (`search schema export|check`)
limits: The index is per machine: device-local on a store machine, `<vault>/.open-second-brain/brain.sqlite` before
An index written by a newer build is refused by an older one with `SCHEMA_MISMATCH`
Refuses a rebuild up front only when both parked copies are kept, one unreadable; `search set-aside` frees one
Only agent activity starts a refresh: no daemon or timer runs index updates

features.name: Semantic search
features.summary: An optional embedding lane beside keyword search, with provider profiles and vector backfill.
capabilities: Embeds chunks through an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint, a provider adapter or an offline hasher
Stores vectors in sqlite-vec (`chunk_vec`) and feeds max(limit x 5, 50) nearest chunks per query into fusion
Walks the operator through the key, sqlite-vec and the first reindex (`embeddings-setup` skill)
Registers named endpoints with env-key failover lists (`search provider add|list|show|remove|presets`)
Refuses a run priced over `embedding_cost_gate_usd` (0 = off) unless `--force-cost`; quotes cost per model
`search vector-backfill` embeds only chunks that have no vector, dry-run unless `--apply`, scoped by `--path`
Stamps the model, dimension, sqlite-vec version and query/passage prefixes on the stored vectors
Warns before a model shutdown from a dated survey or the `embeddings.sunset_at` and `sunset_model` pair
limits: A model, dimension or prefix change drops all stored vectors; the drop is refused while nothing can re-embed
Only `--embeddings`, `vector-backfill`, maintenance and freshen runs with `search_freshen_embeddings` embed
The offline embedder hashes tokens and character trigrams; it matches shared wording, not meaning
Needs a SQLite build that loads extensions; the macOS system SQLite cannot, so a separate one is required

features.name: Search reranking
features.summary: An optional reranker re-scores the top results, with provider profiles, a fit check and a labelled benchmark.
capabilities: Re-scores the top 20 fused candidates (`search_rerank_top_k`) last; off until `search_rerank_enabled`
`search_rerank_kind`: an OpenAI-compatible `/rerank` endpoint, a bundled lexical reranker or a decision model
Falls back to the heuristic order with one telemetry event when the endpoint fails at request time; no retries
Sorts hits under `search_rerank_min_score` last
Runs the decision-model kind in shadow (sent, recorded, order kept) or enforce mode
`search rerank-provider add|list|show|remove` keeps named endpoints: base URL, model, key variable
`search rerank-fit` takes Spearman over up to 12 logged queries: >= 0.15 fits, <= -0.15 inverted
`search rerank-eval` runs a labelled dataset with rerank off and on, reports hit@k and MRR deltas per language
limits: Enabled without a base URL, model and key, the remote kind fails closed with a configuration error
The bundled local reranker scores term coverage, proximity and density; it is not a learned model
`rerank-fit` needs recorded queries in the demand log; without them its verdict is inapplicable
`rerank-eval` recommends enabling only on a pooled MRR or hit@k gain >= 0.01 with no language losing either

features.name: Relational recall
features.summary: An optional fourth search arm that walks typed links and entity co-occurrence under width budgets.
capabilities: Adds a fourth reciprocal-rank-fusion arm when `search_relational_arm_enabled` is on and fusion is `rrf`
Treats a query as relational only if it holds a `[[wikilink]]` seed and a token from the link-type vocabulary
Walks typed edges to depth 2: 8 seeds, 4 edges per node, 16 nodes; hubs over 12 edges are not expanded
Also walks entity co-occurrence bridges by default; `search_entity_bridges_enabled` turns them off
Ranks reached notes by hops, then by edge count
In trust-gate enforce mode, drops arrivals over closed or pending windows or unnamed `contradicts` edges
Stops at the composite recall deadline, keeping the nodes it reached
limits: Off by default, and inert under the default linear fusion even when switched on
Has no verb or tool of its own; it runs inside `search query` and `brain_search`
Walks only edges already in the index and never reads note prose

features.name: Learned ranking and recall focus
features.summary: Relevance feedback trains hybrid ranking weights, a session focus biases recall, and tuning grid-searches parameters.
capabilities: Records up/down verdicts (`search feedback`, `brain_recall_feedback`) as one event each, the query hashed
Captures the judged hit's keyword, semantic, entity and recency scores by re-running the query (top 50)
Folds the events into per-layer multipliers within 0.8-1.2, applied with `search_learned_weights_enabled`
Shows base weights, learned multipliers and the event count (`search weights`)
Biases recall toward a query and path prefix for 120 minutes, globally or per session (`search focus set`)
Scores focus +0.06 or -0.015 on the path prefix, up to +0.04 or -0.01 on terms, clamped to -0.03..+0.08
Grid-searches pool multiplier, traversal depth, learned weights and expansion by MRR (`brain tune run`)
Reports the access activation that ranking boosts by: event, path and co-access counts (`brain activation`)
Answers a remote tuning run without saving its winner; a remote tuning reset keeps the saved tuning
limits: Learned weights and the tuning winner (`Brain/search/tuning.json`) apply only under their flags, default off
Tuning needs an operator-supplied labelled dataset; it does not learn from feedback events
A tuning winner measured while the semantic lane was missing is not saved
A persisted focus is set from the CLI only; MCP callers pass a per-call focus

features.name: Recall benchmarks and telemetry
features.summary: Scores recall against fixed query datasets and fixture vaults, and records opt-in recall telemetry.
capabilities: Scores live hybrid recall on a `{queries: [{id, query, expected}]}` dataset: hit@k and MRR, k=5 by default
`brain benchmark run` appends a `recall_benchmark` metric so recall quality can be charted over time
`brain benchmark run` and `brain_eval` add answer containment@k, source utilization, citation depth, warnings
`brain bench memory` runs ingest, index, retrieve, evaluate, report in a disposable fixture vault, resumable
Ships two public long-term memory benchmark suites and a surfacing-replay suite
Reports quality, latency and context cost separately
Writes one recall-telemetry record per opted-in search, context pack or hook injection: status, hits, gaps
`brain recall-telemetry` lists and summarizes records, gate decisions, write-versus-read cost and dead weight
limits: Benchmarks need an operator-supplied labelled dataset or fixture; nothing is generated from the vault
`brain bench memory` searches keyword-only unless the suite declares the embeddings capability
Telemetry is written only when a call opts in; recall-gate telemetry is off by default

features.name: Session history recall
features.summary: Imports agent transcripts already on disk, searches and expands them, and mines their user turns for signals.
capabilities: Imports Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenCode and Grok transcripts on disk, one file or every known root
Turns `@osb` markers and `brain_feedback` calls in imported transcripts into deduped signals
With `--recall`, stores turns as continuity rows under two levels of extractive summary nodes, 8 sources each
Moves base64 runs and turns over 32,000 chars into `Brain/.payloads/<sha256>.txt`, paged by `brain payload`
Searches imported turns and summaries by substring within a time window (`session-grep`)
Picks turns across a thread's topics within a char budget, optionally entity-seeded (`session-grep` coverage)
Saves the agent's answers to an extraction plan as speculative signals (`extract-signals`)
Scores entity pairs by session co-occurrence (PMI) for promotion into the registry (`brain hallways`)
Re-runs the frozen payload of a half-failed extraction write, dry run first (`brain dead-letters`)
limits: Imports only transcripts already on disk; recall rows exist only for sessions imported with `--recall`
Session grep is case-insensitive substring matching; it does not use the FTS5 or vector index
Summary nodes are extractive, not model-written: 120 chars per turn, 160 per depth-1 node at depth 2
The calling agent extracts signals; an optional `extract_prefilter` decision model may drop turns first
